title: ISO 45001 health and safety (add-on)
description: ISO 45001:2018 on the Core registers: hazard identification and risk assessment with the hierarchy of controls, and worker consultation and participation, with injuries, near misses and ill health in the shared Incidents register, OH&S objectives, risks, nonconformities and documents tagged ISO 45001 with their own views. Full adds contractors, emergency drills and health surveillance. Installs the Core registers first. A new edition of ISO 45001 is expected in 2027: this add-on will get a version on it, and you move your library over from Workspace admin › Frameworks. Written in our own words; no text of the standard.

levels.name: Starter
levels.description: Hazards and OH&S risks (HIRA) and worker consultation, ISO 45001 columns, views and examples on the Core registers, the OH&S risk category and the audit-readiness dashboard.

levels.name: Full
levels.description: Everything in Starter plus contractors, emergency drills and health surveillance (personal data, installed restricted).

sheets.name: Hazards and OH&S risks (HIRA)
sheets.description: Hazard identification and risk assessment: what could hurt someone or make them ill, who is exposed, how likely and how bad it is, the controls in place by the hierarchy of controls (eliminate first, protective equipment last) and the risk that is left. Uses the scales of the OH&S risk category.

fields.name: What could cause harm
fields.description: What could cause harm: a moving part, a chemical, a load, working alone, time pressure.

fields.name: Likelihood
fields.description: Before the controls, on the OH&S category's likelihood scale.

fields.name: Severity
fields.description: Before the controls, on the OH&S category's impact scale.

fields.name: Strongest control
fields.description: The highest level of the hierarchy of controls in place. Work down the list: remove the hazard, replace it, engineer it out, change how the work is done, and only then protective equipment.

fields.name: Workers consulted
fields.description: The people who do the work helped find the hazards and choose the controls.

fields.name: Risk register
fields.description: The risk in the shared risk register this hazard rolls up into, when it matters beyond the task.

rules.message: Record the controls in place, the strongest control and the risk after controls before accepting it.

fields.name: Approval step
fields.description: Where the assessment is in its risk acceptance. Set by the Risk acceptance workflow, never by hand.

items.name: Example: Forklift and pedestrians in the warehouse aisles

values.hazard: Pedestrians walk in the same aisles as forklifts reversing out of racks.
values.controls: Barriers along the main walkway, blue spot lights on forklifts, high-visibility vests.
values.further_controls: Separate pick times for pedestrians in aisle 4; mirrors at the rack ends.

items.name: Example: Solvent-based degreaser in the workshop

values.hazard: Breathing in solvent vapour; skin contact.
values.further_controls: Switch to a water-based degreaser (substitute) and add extraction at the cleaning bench.

items.name: Example: Working alone on the night shift

values.hazard: Nobody notices if the operator is hurt or taken ill.

sheets.name: Worker consultation and participation
sheets.description: How the people who do the work take part: safety committee meetings, toolbox talks, surveys, and the concerns and ideas workers raise, with what was decided and what was done. A concern is answered within 7 days.

fields.name: Answer due
fields.description: Seven days after a concern or idea was raised.

fields.name: Who took part
fields.description: Teams or roles, and the worker representatives.

fields.name: Raised by
fields.description: Optional: a concern can be raised without a name.

rules.message: Write down what was decided or answered before closing it.

layout.description: Tell us about anything at work that could hurt someone or make them ill, or an idea that would make work safer. You do not have to give your name. We answer within 7 days.
layout.nameLabel: Your concern or idea, in one line

fields.label: Is it a concern or an idea?
What did you see, where and when?
Your name (optional)

settings.confirmation: Thank you. Your concern is with the safety team and you will hear back within 7 days.

notice.recipients: The people in this workspace who follow up health and safety concerns.

sheets.name: Contractors
sheets.description: Contractors who work on your sites: the work they do, the safety documents and insurance you checked, their induction and when their approval runs out.

fields.name: Supplier

sheets.name: Emergency drills
sheets.description: Planned and held emergency drills: the scenario, how long it took against the target, what went wrong and what was done about it.

options.label: Rescue from height or a confined space

sheets.name: Health surveillance
sheets.description: Health checks for people exposed to noise, vibration, dust, chemicals or night work: when each person was last seen, when they are due and whether there are work restrictions. Health information about named people: installed restricted, never put clinical details here.

fields.name: Work restrictions
fields.description: Only what the manager needs to know to arrange the work. No diagnosis.

rules.name: Health checks: after the person left the role
rules.note: A suggestion, not advice: some exposure records must be kept for decades and others only for a few years. Your country's rules and your occupational health provider set the period.

items.name: Example: Hearing check for press shop staff

values.likelihood_scale: 1 Rare: not known to have happened in our industry. 2 Unlikely: has happened in our industry. 3 Possible: has happened here or at a similar site. 4 Likely: happens here every year or so. 5 Almost certain: happens here several times a year.
values.impact_scale: 1 Negligible: discomfort, no first aid. 2 Minor: first aid, back at work the same day. 3 Moderate: medical treatment or up to three days off work. 4 Major: more than three days off, a fracture or lasting ill health. 5 Severe: a life-changing injury or a death.

items.name: Example: Serious injury during the summer maintenance shutdown

values.cause: Many contractors at once, non-routine work at height and on isolated machines
values.consequence: A fall or an entanglement, a stopped shutdown and an investigation by the authority

automations.name: OH&S risk above appetite → owner treats it, the HSE manager is told
automations.description: Escalation: when an ISO 45001 risk's score rises above 4 (the OH&S category's appetite) and it is above its category's appetite, the risk owner is asked to plan the treatment and the HSE manager is told.

actions.message: {id} {name} scores {score}, above the appetite of its category. Plan the treatment and set a review date.
{id} {name} is above appetite (score {score}). The risk owner has been asked to treat it.

notice.recipients: The people in this workspace who investigate incidents.
notice.retention: Kept for 5 years after the incident is closed, or longer where the law requires it.

automations.name: Incident reportable to the authority → tell the HSE manager
automations.description: SLA clock: when an incident is marked reportable, the HSE manager and the investigator are told at once, because the authority has to be told within a legal time limit (check the limit where you work).

actions.message: {id} {name} on {occurred_on} is reportable. Tell the authority within the legal time limit and record when you did.

automations.name: Time off work after an incident → raise a nonconformity and tell top management
automations.description: Escalation and cascade: when days off work are recorded on an incident, a linked nonconformity tagged ISO 45001 is raised for the root cause and corrective action, and top management are told: lost-time injuries are a management review input.

actions.message: {id} {name} led to {iso45001_days_lost} days off work. A nonconformity has been raised for the investigation.

items.name: How we identify hazards and assess risks

automations.name: Hazard review in 30 days → ask the owner

actions.message: Review {id} {name} by {review_date}: is the hazard still there, do the controls work and has anything changed?

automations.name: Risk after controls 12 or more → stop and tell the HSE manager
automations.description: Escalation: a hazard whose risk after controls reaches 12 (High) is marked Needs more controls and the HSE manager and the owner are told, because work should not go on with a high risk left.

actions.message: {id} {name} is still High after controls (score {residual}). Add stronger controls before the work goes on.

automations.name: Protective equipment as the strongest control on a serious hazard → ask for a better control
automations.description: Hierarchy of controls gate: when protective equipment is the strongest control on a hazard whose risk before controls is 10 or more, the owner is asked to look for elimination, substitution or an engineering control, and the hazard cannot be accepted until the reason is noted.

actions.message: {id} {name} relies on protective equipment alone. Can the hazard be removed, replaced or engineered out? Write why not under Further controls needed.
Protective equipment is the last control in the hierarchy: look for a stronger one before accepting this risk.

automations.name: Risk accepted → next review in a year
automations.description: Recurring review cycle: when a hazard's risk is accepted, its next review is set a year ahead, so every assessment is looked at again at least once a year (sooner after an incident or a change).

automations.name: Concern answer due in 2 days → tell the follow-up owner
automations.description: SLA clock, step 1: a safety concern or idea is answered within 7 days. Two days before the answer is due, the person following it up is reminded.

actions.message: {id} {name}: the worker who raised it should hear back by {answer_due}.

automations.name: Concern not answered in 7 days → tell the HSE manager
automations.description: SLA clock, step 2: a safety concern or idea with no answer after 7 days goes to the HSE manager the next day, so workers see that raising a concern leads somewhere.

actions.message: {id} {name} was raised on {held_on} and has no answer yet.

automations.name: Consultation needs action → create an action
automations.description: Cascade: ticking Needs action on a meeting, a talk or a concern creates a linked action in Actions, tagged ISO 45001 and due in 30 days, so what was agreed with workers is followed up like any other action.

automations.name: Contractor approval expires in 30 days → ask our contact

actions.message: The approval of {name} expires on {approval_expires}. Collect a current method statement and insurance and submit it for approval again.

automations.name: Contractor insurance expires → suspend and tell our contact
automations.description: Gate: the day before a contractor's insurance evidence expires, an approved contractor is suspended and our contact told, so nobody works on site without cover.

actions.message: {name} is suspended: the insurance evidence has expired. Upload the new certificate and approve them again.

automations.name: Drill in 7 days → tell the drill lead

actions.message: {name} is planned for {planned_on}. Brief the observers and set the target time.

automations.name: Drill closed → plan the next one in six months
automations.description: Recurring drill cycle: when a drill is closed, the next drill is planned six months ahead with the same lead, so drills keep happening without anyone having to remember.

automations.name: Health check due in 30 days → ask who arranges it

actions.message: {id} {name} is due on {next_check}. Book it with the provider and set the status to Booked.

automations.name: Health check date passed → mark it overdue and tell the HSE manager
automations.description: Escalation: the day after a health check was due and not done, it is marked Overdue and the HSE manager is told along with whoever arranges it, so exposed people are not left without surveillance.

actions.message: {id} {name} was due on {next_check} and has not been done.

setup.title: ISO 45001 setup
setup.description: Four steps to a health and safety system an auditor can follow, on the shared registers.

steps.title: Decide what applies
steps.body: Mark every ISO 45001 requirement applicable or not, with a reason for the ones that are not.

steps.title: Assess your hazards with the people who do the work
steps.body: Walk through each task with the people who do it, list the hazards, the controls in place by the hierarchy of controls and the risk that is left, and get each one accepted.

steps.title: Show how workers take part
steps.body: Log your safety committee meetings and toolbox talks, and share the concern form with everyone.

target.view: Raise a safety concern or idea

steps.title: Test your emergency response
steps.body: Plan drills for the emergencies you could face and record how each one went.

starter.title: Decide how you test your emergency response
starter.body: Starter has no drill log: record in the library how you plan and test emergency drills, or add Full for the Emergency drills sheet.
